compose.NOT_A_STATEMENT_ABOUT_ADMISSIBILITY: compose is arithmetic on operator indices only. It implies NOTHING about whether the collapsed operator is admissible between the first source and the last target: see is_admissible.witnesses.no_composition_law. It is also NOT the book's composition of operator sequences, which the book says is not commutative (DR-7).
compose.WARNING: Commutative and associative. A modular sum solves any nested repetition WITHOUT preserving grouping or operand order, so success here is NOT evidence of order-sensitive expression reasoning (directive s9). Use as a conformance test and as a strong baseline only.
algebraic_properties: every element invertible: compose(k, (10-k)%10) == 0 -- this is a GROUP (Z/10), not merely a monoid
compose.authoritative_definition: operators.rs doc comment, quoted: 'Monoid composition. CO-0 is the identity element. composition maps (CO-a, CO-b) -> CO-((a+b) mod 10)' -- CO-k is the engine's spelling of ^k
compose.implementation_locator: impl CognitiveOperator :: fn compose(self, other) ; cas-native COMPOSE_TABLE[i][j] = (i + j) % 10

witnesses.note: zero: compose is commutative, which is why it is conformance-only

depends on operator, both domains and the target noetic

is_admissible.authoritative_definition: project instructions, CORRECTION 1: each operator ^k has an admissibility relation D_k over states; D_0 is the diagonal only

expected_cases.reading: the book says this single step is impossible; the engine allows it (DR-5)
^2 then ^8 are each admissible, compose(2,8) = 0, and ^0 from P1 to P2 is not

is_admissible.implementation_locator: impl CognitiveOperator :: fn is_admissible(self, source: CognitiveStateId, target: CognitiveStateId) -> bool
is_admissible.role_in_the_lab: THE order-sensitive operation: source and target are not interchangeable and the answer depends on context
semantics_as_read_from_code: ^k (k != 0), different domains: true iff target.operator == k

no_composition_law.reading: two admissible steps do NOT make the collapsed operator admissible. Not a defect of the code, which promises no such law; a generator or a learner that assumes it is wrong.

witnesses.note: a (source, target) pair is context-sensitive when the answer depends on WHICH operator is applied

rpm_embed_realize.KNOWN_LIMIT_OF_THE_FROZEN_ENGINE: rpm/mod.rs RpmState and ontology/states.rs CognitiveStateVector derive serde Deserialize without re-running their constructors' checks, and CognitiveStateVector's PartialEq zips without a length check. Nothing in the repository loads those types from outside data today. A `satisfied` flag or a state vector is trustworthy only when built through the constructor.
rpm_embed_realize.NOTE_NOT_THE_SAME_AS: cas-native/model/rpm_gate.py PrerequisiteGateLayer, whose docstring says 'the section law epsilon o eta = id is not hard-constrained'. That layer is a TRAINABLE mechanism and is NOT an admitted operation (directive s7). Recorded as discrepancy DR-2.
rpm_embed_realize.WHAT_THE_SECTION_LAW_DOES_NOT_SHOW: realize returns the first coordinate of (s, s*s, sqrt s), so the section law holds by construction. It is a regression test for exact recovery. It is not evidence that a learned encoder found a meaningful representation.
algebraic_properties: section law eps o eta = id on [0,1]
retraction FAILS in general: eta(eps(e)) != e -- asserted, not tolerated
one-directional: prerequisite satisfaction is cached, never re-derived by round trip
rpm_embed_realize.authoritative_definition: project instructions, CORRECTION 2: RPM is a section-retraction, NOT an adjunction: eps o eta = id, but eta o eps != id
rpm_embed_realize.implementation_locator: pub fn embed(score: f64) -> (s, s*s, sqrt s) ; pub fn realize(&EmbeddedScore) -> components[0] ; verify_section_law tolerance f64::EPSILON * 2.0
rpm_embed_realize.invalid_input: INVALID_INPUT (engine: ScoreOutOfRange) for NaN or outside [0, 1]
rpm_embed_realize.numerical_policy: floating point. embed and realize are exact operations; the SECTION LAW is asserted at |realize(embed(s)) - s| <= 2 * f64::EPSILON = 4.440892098500626e-16, exactly the engine's tolerance. This is the only admitted operation with a tolerance, and the tolerance is the engine's, not the lab's.
rpm_embed_realize.role_in_the_lab: fixed; the one op with a numerical policy; the retraction-failure direction is a required negative case
